result.spec:
Value bubbles on the Map page (B6): placement, counts and data format. Source: the local reference build at /home/user/hail-b5/out/ref/site, block view centred on 46.86016, -113.99992, 390 by 844 CSS px at 2x.

1. Bottom line
- A bubble on every house does not fit at zoom 17, the Map page's top zoom. Giving each house its own bubble and skipping any bubble that overlaps a placed one by more than 2 px shows 91 of 248 houses (37%). Drawing all 248 would give 505 overlapping pairs.
- Recommended: one bubble per cluster of houses. Houses in the same 1 km cell that lie within one label width (56 px) of a cluster's first house form one cluster. Each cluster gets one bubble above or below the house nearest its middle. At zoom 17 that is 56 bubbles, and all 248 houses sit in a cluster with a bubble. At zoom 18 (a what-if, see section 6) it is 34 bubbles for 69 houses.
- Which reads better: the cluster version. It is quieter (56 bubbles, against 91 per-house bubbles that still leave 157 houses with no bubble, which reads as no value). It also shows the data as it is: one value per cell, not one per house. The per-house version repeats one number across neighbouring houses and suggests a house-level figure the data does not hold. Its cost: a bubble covers at least part of the dot of 114 of 248 houses at zoom 17 (134 in the per-house version). The outlines stay visible.
- Decision for the owner: 'a value bubble on every house' needs either overlapping bubbles (505 pairs at zoom 17, the reference app's style) or the cluster rule. I recommend the cluster rule.

2. What was read
- The page fetched six building shards for the view. Four hold the 248 dots in view: r0081_c0159131 (15 dots), r0081_c01591331 (112), r0081_c0160020 (11), r0081_c01600220 (110). The other two serve only the margin. The page fetches no cell shards at draw time, so the browser holds no values today.
- Projection: Web Mercator, 256 x 2^zoom px. The dot centres match the owner's capture to within 0.1 image px (mean offset 0.13 and -0.05 px).
- Four 0.01 degree cells are in view: rows 813 and 814, columns 1599 and 1600. Each cell's value is the largest stored radar estimate of 0.25 in or more (64 tenths of a mm) in the window 2021-10-17 to 2026-10-16. That is the rule of hail.py describe and summary.py (largest value over the five seasons). Inches are floored to the hundredth (100 x tenths // 254).
  - r813_c1599: 0.38 in (62 houses)
  - r814_c1599: '--' (65 houses; no stored estimate of 0.25 in or more)
  - r813_c1600: 0.30 in (55 houses)
  - r814_c1600: 0.26 in (66 houses)
  Checked twice: with the helper code and with a separate read of the two cell shards.
- The index lists one missing day in the window, 2022-06-08. That day has no estimate in any cell, so a largest value could be understated. The sheet should say so.
- A cell is about 1.1 km north to south and 0.8 km east to west (0.01 degree).

3. Bubble geometry (CSS px, site tokens only)
- Text: 13 px, weight 700, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next from website/static/fonts, tabular figures, letter-spacing -0.02 em (-0.26 px a character). Widths were measured with Pillow on that font at 26 px and halved. '0.38 in' is 43.57 px before letter-spacing.
- Body: 22 px high, pill radius 11 px, 7 px padding each side, minimum width 30 px. '0.38 in' bubbles are 55.75 px wide; '--' bubbles are 30 px.
- Pointer: 8 px wide and 5 px tall, its tip 1 px above the dot's top edge. The dot radius is 4 px at zoom 17 and 18, from the build's rule min(4.0, 2.5 + 0.5 x (zoom - 13)). A bubble below its house mirrors this.
- Light colours: fill --ink-950 (#111c28), text --white (#ffffff), a 1.5 px --white halo. A tapped (selected) house: fill --sky-700 (#1a5a9c) and a 2 px --sky-700 ring on its dot.
- Dark colours (proposal, not rendered): fill --mist-100, text --night-950, selected --sky-300. Check in a dark capture before shipping.
- No hazard colour is used, so no hazard word is needed.
- The existing town bubbles use map.css --bubble (rgba(74, 74, 79, 0.9)), which is not a style.css token. The map would then carry two bubble colours. Decide whether the town bubbles move to --ink-950 too.
- Overlap test: two boxes clash when they overlap by more than 2 px in both directions. A box is the bubble body plus its pointer.

4. Placement rules (fixed for each house, independent of the view and of taps)
- Order: dots with a value first, largest value first, then the '--' dots. Ties go north to south, then west to east, then by shard name and index.
- Per house (rule A): the bubble above the dot, skipped when it clashes with a placed bubble. Rule A2 also tries below the dot: 104 bubbles at zoom 17 and 60 at zoom 18.
- Cluster (rule B, recommended): within one 1 km cell, a house joins the nearest leader within 56 px. A leader is the first house in north-to-south, west-to-east order that started its group. The anchor is the house nearest the group's middle. Place the bubble above the anchor, else below, else skip. Same order as rule A.
- Outlines outside the hail grid get no bubble. They never get '--'.
- Reach check at zoom 17 (cluster rule): 28 px gives 86 bubbles and 174 houses covered (70%); 40 px gives 75 and 231 (93%); 56 px gives 56 and 248 (100%), largest group 86 px (about 70 m); 80 px gives 36 and 248, largest 129 px (about 105 m); 112 px gives 23 and 248, largest 197 px (about 160 m). A chained variant (houses whose boxes overlap join one group) gives 23 bubbles for 229 houses, with up to 27 houses in one bubble. That is too coarse.
- Whole-tile check: the placement over all 33,162 outlines of the two tiles gives the same view counts (56 and 248 at zoom 17; 34 and 69 at zoom 18), so the placement does not depend on the viewport here.

5. Counts
Zoom 17: 248 houses in view (183 with a value, 65 '--').
- Per house (rule A): 91 bubbles (37%), 66 with a value and 25 '--'. By cell: r813_c1599 21 of 62; r814_c1599 25 of 65; r813_c1600 22 of 55; r814_c1600 23 of 66.
- Clusters (rule B): 56 bubbles, all 248 houses covered; 42 value bubbles and 14 '--'. Anchors by cell: r813_c1599 13; r813_c1600 14; r814_c1599 14; r814_c1600 15. Houses per bubble: 1 (4 bubbles), 2 (4), 3 (11), 4 (17), 5 (7), 6 (4), 7 (5), 8 (3), 9 (1). Nine bubbles sit below their house. Largest group 86 px (about 70 m), median 49 px (about 40 m).
Zoom 18 (what-if): 69 houses in view (53 with a value, 16 '--').
- Per house: 52 bubbles (75%). By cell: r813_c1599 15 of 22; r813_c1600 10 of 14; r814_c1599 13 of 16; r814_c1600 14 of 17.
- Clusters: 34 bubbles, all 69 houses covered. Anchors by cell: r813_c1599 10; r813_c1600 8; r814_c1599 7; r814_c1600 9. Houses per bubble: 1 (6), 2 (22), 3 (5), 4 (1). Largest group 73 px (about 30 m).

6. Zoom 18
The Map page cannot reach zoom 18 today. Its maximum zoom is the larger of the view's own limit (11) and the buildings' top zoom, which is 17, so the page stops at 17 (checked in the browser: asking for 18 returned 17). The zoom 18 counts and pictures come from a test session that lifts that limit for the test only. Nothing in the site changed. Whether the top zoom rises is the owner's call.

7. Data format
Option A (recommended): Python writes label flags into each building shard.
- Shape: a new header key 'lb' on each hail/b shard, holding f: 'hail-labels-v1', z: [17, 18], k: one digit per outline, and c: a table from 'row,col' to label text. Digit = 3 x code17 + code18, where code 0 is no bubble, 1 an anchor with its bubble above, and 2 an anchor with its bubble below. Digits follow the shard's outline order. The c table lists each cell that has an outline in the shard.
- Browser: for each outline whose digit is not 0 at the current zoom, draw the bubble at its dot with the pointer on the coded side, taking the text from c under the cell of the dot (the grid arithmetic the browser already has, hailCell). About 30 lines. No placement and no text measurement. A tapped house gets a sky-700 ring on its dot; its bubble turns sky-700 when the house is an anchor.
- Measured on the four view shards (2,114 outlines): raw 503,993 to 506,566 bytes (+2,573, +0.5%); gzip level 6: 78,498 to 79,938 (+1,440, +1.8%). That is 1.2 raw and 0.7 gzip bytes per outline. Raw additions per shard: +1,018 (881 outlines), +452 (362), +721 (584), +382 (287). The digits cover zoom 18 too. A zoom 17 only key would be shorter; it was not measured separately.
- Build: the placement runs once per build. The two-tile check took about 80 s with a simple overlap test on 33,162 outlines. The full state (918,052 outlines) needs a spatial grid index for the overlap test. The full-state run time is not measured.

Option B (browser thinning at draw time): the browser places bubbles on every pan and zoom.
- Needs: the cell values, which the page does not fetch today (the two cell shards for this view, r0081_c0159.json at 2,654 bytes and r0081_c0160.json at 3,404 bytes: 6,058 bytes raw, 2,048 gzip). The largest-in-window rule would run in JavaScript, which docs/DESIGN.md section 9 (principle 4) forbids, unless Python also writes a per-cell maximum table. Leader clustering per cell, the two-anchor box test and the order (about 50 lines of JavaScript), label widths from canvas measureText (which must agree with Python within the 2 px tolerance), and the constants passed in from Python.
- Behaviour: placement depends on which houses are on screen, so labels can appear or move while the map pans.
- Bytes: about 6 KB raw of extra fetch per view plus the code, against 2.6 KB raw added to the four shards with no extra fetch.

Recommendation: Option A. Python does the work (AGENTS.md rule 4), it costs about 0.7 gzip bytes per outline, the browser only draws, and each label stays put as the map moves. Option B would also need the largest-value rule in JavaScript.

8. Words (Python writes them under rule 4; these are proposals, not in the modules)
- Bubble: '0.38 in' (the largest radar estimate for the cell over five years).
- Dash: '--' means no radar estimate of 0.25 in or more is stored for this cell in these five years. Sheet sentence: 'No radar estimate of 0.25 in or more is stored for this cell in these five years. That is not the same as no hail.'
- Cluster sentence on the sheet: 'Every building in this cell shares this value. It is a radar estimate for the cell, about 1.1 km north to south and 0.8 km east to west, not a measurement at this building.'
- Missing day sentence, when the window has a missing day: 'One day in these five years has no radar data (Jun 8, 2022).'

9. Interaction
- Bubbles take no taps (pointer-events none), so a tap falls through to the nearest dot within 12 px, as now. A tap on a dot opens its sheet. Every house in one cell shows the same value on its sheet.
- A tapped anchor's bubble turns sky-700. A tapped house inside another house's group gets the sky-700 ring on its dot only.

10. Not done or not verified
- Bubble widths come from Pillow measurements of the site font, not from a browser render. Check in Chromium before shipping.
- Dark mode was not rendered.
- Reach was checked for this one view. Other views and dense cells may leave a group without a bubble. The build should count and report that.
- The four pictures are Pillow drawings over the captures, with letter-spacing applied per character. Expect about 1 px of difference in the browser.
- bubbles.md was not written (see problems). The full text is this spec.

problems: Evidence honesty, the dash label: '--' is shown for r814_c1599 (65 houses; 25 per-house bubbles and 14 cluster bubbles at zoom 17). That cell has no stored entry at all in the five-year window, so it is a 'no estimate' case, and a bare dash reads like an all-clear (AGENTS rule 5). Use the words the site already defines in website/hail.py WORDS ('No day between ... has a radar-estimated hail size of 0.25 in or more at this spot. That is not the same as no hail ...'). Reserve the site's unavailable words (hail.py 'unavailable') for a tile or key that cannot be read. The site's own dash convention in map.js (a dash with visually hidden words) is not used either.

No label says what the number is. Each bubble shows only '0.38 in'. DESIGN section 9 requires, beside every number on the sheet and town tables, the kind (a radar estimate of the largest hail over the cell, during the day) and what it is not (not a measurement, not an inspection, not a sign of no hail). The spec gives no legend, no window (2021-10-17 to 2026-10-16) and no date for the largest day (2024-08-15 for the 0.38 in cell). DESIGN also says the hail legend line 'is not a size key'; sized bubbles on the map need that decision made again by the owner.

Missing day and stale store are not shown. index.json lists 2022-06-08 as the one missing day in the window, so the largest values can be understated; DESIGN requires 'Days with no data, not counted' beside the rows. The newest day is 2026-10-16, nine days before today (2026-10-25). DESIGN's stale rule is more than three days, so the stale words apply. The spec has no as-of date and no stale state.

Coverage claim is overstated at zoom 17. The spec says 56 cluster bubbles 'cover all 248 houses in view'. Counting only what is on screen (390 x 844), 239 of 248 in-view houses have a visible bubble. Nine (six at 0.38 in, three at the dash) sit in clusters whose bubble lies entirely off-screen (anchors at y = -6 and y = 844.6). At zoom 18 all 69 are covered. Either place a visible bubble for every in-view cluster or state 239 of 248.

The 'one value per cell' reason does not hold. The cluster rule shows each cell's value on 13 to 15 bubbles (56 bubbles for four values). Each pointer ends on one house, so each bubble reads as that house's figure, which is the house-level reading the spec rejects for the per-house version. Test a per-cell label (four labels in this view) before the owner decides. The B6 brief (task 38) asks for a value bubble per house, so the cluster rule is a departure. The spec marks it as the owner's decision, which is right, but the reason it gives should be corrected.

Clipped labels. At zoom 17, 13 of 64 visible cluster bubbles and 23 of 103 visible per-house bubbles are cut by the frame edge. A cut value such as '.38 in' or '0.3' can be misread. Keep every label fully on screen, or hide a label that would be cut.

Pills can touch. The clash test counts an overlap only when it is more than 2 px on both axes, so pills can overlap by up to 2 px along one axis. In the per-house version 9 pairs of visible pills touch (depth up to 1.7 px). Require a real gap of a few pixels.

The data format is missing from the spec as received. The text stops inside the colour section ('a 1.5 px -.') and cites a section 6 that is not in it. The worker's candidate format (bubbles/format_bytes.py, shards-candidate/) adds one code per outline and a cell table. Putting the codes in Python is right, but its text comes from extract.py's own inch function, not website/hail.py WORDS. Every sentence the site shows must be a WORDS template (hail.py header; DESIGN section 9 principle 4), so '0.38 in', the dash and the no-estimate words need WORDS entries. The browser must not do the 100 x tenths // 254 arithmetic (the map.js header says it holds no unit).

Scope of the data format and the placement. The candidate covers only the two tiles that hold this view (r0081_c0159 and r0081_c0160). The pictures use a placement computed per view (houses in view plus an 80 px margin, sorted on screen), while the candidate is computed per tile. The spec does not say which one ships, how bubbles move on pan, what happens at a tile edge, or from which zoom bubbles show. Zoom 15 and 16 are untested, and dots already start at zoom 15 (DESIGN section 10).

Cost is measured on four shards only. The candidate adds about 1.2 bytes per outline raw and about 0.7 bytes gzipped (2,114 outlines in the four shards). The store index counts about 918,000 footprints, so the same rule would add roughly 1.1 MB raw and 0.6 MB gzipped state-wide, which was not measured. The phone view is at 682,129 bytes gzipped against the 700,000 budget (ROADMAP), and the store already breaks its caps (B5 at about 162 MB against 60 MB; the owner rules on it).

Dark mode is not checked. All four pictures are light. DESIGN's contrast table requires computed contrast for every token pair in light and dark. The spec uses the primitives --ink-950 and --white, not the map's own bubble tokens (--bubble, --bubble-text, --bubble-ring and --bubble-unknown in website/static/map/map.css, with dark variants). No dark value is given.

Geometry is drawn with Pillow, not in a browser. The pictures are Pillow overlays on a Chromium capture, and no bubble exists in the site yet. In Chromium with the site font (13 px, weight 700, -0.02 em, tabular figures) the '0.38 in' pill is 55.19 px, not the 55.75 px the spec gives. The dash pill is 30 px because the site sets border-box sizing globally, so that figure is right. AGENTS rule 8 needs a real in-page render before the placements are used.

The reference-app style is no longer a reason. The spec argues that overlapping bubbles (505 pairs) are the reference app's style, and the owner has now said that base is not wanted in the finish. That argument should be dropped, and the choice made on legibility and evidence alone. DECISIONS D28 and DESIGN section 8 still describe the map in that base's style, so the owner needs to decide the replacement (not edited here).

The base images are mislabelled. The spec calls the pictures 'the owner's block capture' and says the dot centres match 'the owner's capture' to 0.1 px. Smaller points: (a) '1 km cell' should be the 0.01 degree cell, about 1.1 km by 0.8 km (DESIGN: 0.7 by 0.5 miles). (b) The spec's prose says 'house' throughout; DESIGN section 10 bans 'house' in templates (the bubble text itself has no such word). strengths: The counts reproduce exactly. In a copy of the worker's pipeline (extract, place, clusters, draw, final), two runs are byte-identical and match the worker's placements and final.json: 248 in-view houses; 62, 55, 65 and 66 per cell; 15, 112, 11 and 110 per shard; 91 per-house bubbles; 505 overlapping pairs; 134 and 114 dots under bubbles; 56 cluster bubbles. The cell values hold against the store. r813_c1599 is 0.38 in (99 tenths on 2024-08-15), r813_c1600 is 0.30 in (78 tenths, same day), r814_c1600 is 0.26 in (67 tenths on 2025-06-12), and r814_c1599 has no stored entry. The inch rule (100 x tenths // 254) and the 64-tenth floor match hail.py.

Cell and key arithmetic matches DESIGN section 9 and hail.py: row = floor(5500 - 100 x lat), col = floor(100 x lon + 13000), key = (row % 10) x 10 + col % 10. The per-cell and per-shard house counts were recounted from the raw building shards in hail/b, independent of the worker's files.

The projection is right. All 248 in-view dots match a rendered dot in the Chromium capture (Web Mercator, 256 x 2^zoom px). After a half-pixel pixel-centre correction the mean offset is about 0.01 CSS px or less, the 95th percentile 0.06 px and the maximum 0.37 px.

The colours and type come from the site. --ink-950 (#111c28), --white (#ffffff) and --sky-700 (#1a5a9c) exist in website/static/style.css with the stated values. White on ink is about 17:1 and white on sky-700 about 7:1. The 13 px, weight 700, -0.02 em, tabular type matches the site's own map bubble in map.css, and the site's own woff2 loads in Chromium. Tabular figures work: 0.25, 0.26, 0.30, 0.38 and 1.00 in all measure 55.19 px.

The dot radius rule (2.5 px at zoom 13, plus 0.5 px a zoom, capped at 4 px) matches DOT_RADIUS_PX in website/addresses.py. The six building shards fetched for the view match the capture log, and the other two hold no in-view dots. The bubble text carries its unit ('in').

The spec is open about its trade-off. It gives the per-house and cluster counts, the 114 of 248 dot coverage and the 505 pairs, and marks the rule as the owner's decision. The placement is deterministic, and the candidate format is small (about 1.2 bytes per outline raw on the four shards measured).
